text:
Bad Creek Project would be able to generate 32 hours at full load with the 30,228 acre-feet of storage provided in the upper reservoir. Typically, generation would begin on Monday with the upper reservoir at maximum elevation, and each weekday power would be generated during peak periods of system demand. During the off-peak hours, a portion of the water would be pumped back into the upper reservoir. Such an operation during weekdays would result in a net reduction of storage in the upper reservoir that would be replaced by weekend pumping. During peak demand weeks, the water surface of the upper reservoir could fluctuate between elevations of 2,310 and 2,150 feet, a drawdown of 160 feet (Figure 1-12). Assuming full output generating, the rate of drawdown from full reservoir would be 2.5 feet per hour during the first hour and 12.5 feet per hour for the last. The maximum average daily rate of drawdown would be about 8.3 feet.
To maintain the downstream aquatic habitat in Bad Creek, water could be released through a control structure to be provided at the downstream toe of the main dam. A 12-inch steel pipe would be embedded in concrete in a trench excavated in rock under the dam. The inlet control structure would permit water to be withdrawn from three different elevations. The outlet end of the pipe would be fitted with an aerator and control valve, so that release could be controlled to duplicate as closely as possible the quality of natural discharge. A 48-inch diameter steel pipe would be embedded in the same trench for diversion of the natural flow from the Bad Creek drainage during construction and would be plugged after completion of construction.
To drain the power tunnel for inspection, the reservoir would be drawn down to 2,124 feet. The intake channel would be provided with a retaining structure equipped with sluice gates. When the gates are closed, they would retain enough water to refill the power tunnel after an inspection is completed.
No pollutants would be discharged from plant operation. Sewage generated at the project would be treated in accordance with State laws.
Since the drainage area of Bad Creek is small, it would not be practical to fill the upper reservoir by natural inflow. Therefore, the filling would be done by pumping from Jocassee Reservoir when the first unit is tested.
